messages.subject: unbundle instructions?
messages.body_plain:
I have used R to combine data from disparate sources into a database. I am now preparing to publish the database, and will include the R code and source files I used to create the database as an appendix to make the database fully reproducible. I also used packrat (v 0.4.8-1) to create a packrat snapshot of my package dependencies, and then create a bundle for sharing the package dependencies. I want to also make the R environment reproducible for database users by providing the packrat bundle and instructions to database users for how to use it. The packrat documentation for how to initialize packrat, take the snapshot, and create the bundle was great.

However, I am struggling with how to use the undbundled snapshot, and how to develop clear instructions for using the bundle to potential R code users. To test out unbundling, I attempted to unbundle the snapshot and then run R code on a different computer (with newer versions or R, R studio, and Mac OS) than the computer I used to write the R code and create the bundle. I called library(packrat) and packrat::unbundle(bundle = "directory", where = "directory"), which worked fine. But subsequently packrat::restore() gave me the error "This project has not yet been packified. Run 'packrat::init()' to init packrat". Is it really necessary to create a new packrat project in order to access a bundle? (that doesn't make sense to me). I have had difficulty troubleshooting this problem because the packrat page (https://rstudio.github.io/packrat/) and cran provide very little documentation about unbundling and how to utilize an unbundled snapshot (at least from my perspective).

So, can someone please provide clear step-by-step instructions for how to unbundle an saved snapshot, and then use that snapshot to run R code? Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: unbundle instructions?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jason,

Are you able to provide any more information? Things should work just fine as you describe; that is, calling

    packrat::unbundle(<project>, where = <dir>)

should automatically unbundle and restore the project. After that, attempting to launch an R process in the <dir>/<project> folder should then be launched in 'packrat mode' for that project, using the private project R library. Note that the bundled project will be unpacked into a directory within <dir> specified above; not directly into that <dir>.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.subject: Re: unbundle instructions?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Kevin. After reading your response, I discovered my problems were that a) I was expecting to see both user and system libraries in R after running the unbundle code (still just saw systems library in R studio after executing the unbundle command), and b) I already had a folder with the same name of the bundled project folder in the directory specified in the 'where' statement of the unbundle command, so I didn't realize anything happened. However, as you pointed out, when I opened project R code files within the directory created through the unbundle in R studio, the user libraries with the project's package dependencies appeared. So, everything was working, and I was just confused.

It appears different commands are needed to access the project package dependencies depending on how the bundle (tar file) is handled by bundle users? If bundle users run an unbundle command in R, the entire project directory is expanded and all R code files within the project access the user library with the project's package dependencies when they are open, and thus users could execute the R code using the project's package dependencies without any additional action beyond the undbundle command. In contrast, if bundle users expand the tar on their own using a mac or a program such as 7-zip, the project folder will be expanded, but opening R code files within the project will not result in the project library to be directly accessible; rather, it appears a packrat::restore() command must be executed, and then R must be re-started?

For my purposes, these kind of distinctions are important...I expect my bundle users to be familiar with R and R studio, but likely will not have experience with packrat. So, to take a stab at answering my own question...it seems one approach might be to provide bundle users a) the bundle (tar file), b) an R script with unbundle code, and c) a README.txt file that includes instructions such as:

i) execute the unbundle.R script using R studio
ii) close R studio
iii) open R files within the project directory created by the unbundle command in R studio, which also allows the R script to utilize the project's package dependencies (user library rather than system library)
v) run the project R scripts, which will execute the scripts using the project's package dependencies.

messages.subject: Re: packrat and package development
messages.body_plain:
Does anyone know if this has been done? I haven't spotted anything in the current documentation yet.

On Wednesday, 25 June 2014 00:05:08 UTC+1, Kevin Ushey wrote:
> Hi Erik,
>
> This is definitely something we want to add into Packrat, but there is still a ways to go -- more R package support is something we hope to tackle in the next release.
>
> Best,
> Kevin
>
> On Friday, June 20, 2014 9:28:41 PM UTC-7, Erik Iverson wrote:
> > Hello,
> >
> > The current documentation for packrat mentions working on R 'projects' extensively, which I interpret to mean data analyses that you'd like to ensure remain reproducible in the short and long term. That's a great concept, but I'm wondering if packrat is useful for R package development, as a sort of replacement for the Description file's Depends/Imports keywords? As more and more packages spring up on Github and not necessarily on CRAN, it seems it would be useful to be able to specify that Github PackageA that I'm working on depends on another Github PackageB and I'm working on and Github PackageC that a colleague is working on. I've got to study the docs more, but perhaps when PackageC is updated, there are options to either keep up the PackageA library up-to-date with the latest PackageC commit, or specify a particular commit of PackageC to depend on.
> >
> > Thanks!
> > --Erik
